podcast.body: This song became Mariah Carey's ninth number one hit, out of a career total of 19, in September 1995. It was historic for several reasons, being one of the first sample-based pop songs to top the Hot 100 and, in its remix featuring Ol' Dirty Bastard, it helped establish the rap and R&B duet. Most notably, Fantasy was the first song by a female artist and one of the first songs overall to debut at number one on the Hot 100, which had never happened before 1995 for a female artist. Unlike Michael Jackson's "You Are Not Alone," "Fantasy" turned out to be a massive and well-loved hit, spending eight weeks at number one through the fall of 1995 and setting up an even bigger follow-up hit. "Fantasy was historic for several reasons. It was one of the first sample based pop songs to top the hot 100."
